## Dataset: SnowTinel high-temporal-resolution ground truth dataset for SAR remote sensing of snow

This dataset consists of a series of full snow profiles collected at the Weissfluhjoch field site in Davos, Switzerland, over the two snow seasons of 2022-2023 and 2023-2024. This series of snow profiles was collected at high vertical and temporal resolution, with a specific focus on the melting seasons, during which up to 3 profiles per week were sampled. This dataset is part of the measurement campaign conducted within the SnowTinel project, which aims to explore the Sentinel-1 SAR backscattering response to melting Alpine snowpacks. Therefore, this dataset contains manual measurements of the main properties of snow that are responsible for scattering, i.e., temperature, density, specific surface area &#40;SSA&#41;, liquid water content &#40;LWC&#41;, surface roughness, and snow water equivalent &#40;SWE&#41;. <br>The dataset comprises 85 snow profiles: 38 carried out in 2022-2023 and 47 in 2023-2024. <br>  - Profiles of snow &#42;&#42;temperature&#42;&#42; were sampled at a vertical resolution of 10 cm &#40;2022-2023&#41; and 5 cm &#40;2023-2024&#41; using HI98501 Checktemp from Hanna Instruments;<br>   - Profiles of snow &#42;&#42;density&#42;&#42; were sampled at a vertical resolution of 3 cm using a box density cutter and a digital scale;<br>   - Profiles of snow &#42;&#42;specific surface area&#42;&#42; were sampled at a vertical resolution of 4 cm using the InfraSnow sensor from FPGA;<br>   - Profiles of snow &#42;&#42;liquid water content&#42;&#42; were sampled at a vertical resolution of 2 cm using the Denothmeter &#40;2022-2023&#41; and the New Capacitive Sensor from FPGA &#40;2023-2024&#41;. In conditions of ripe snow, dielectric measurements were backed up by melting calorimetry measurements following a recently revised field protocol;<br>   - Snow &#42;&#42;surface roughness&#42;&#42; is expressed by the Root Mean Square of the Heights &#40;RMSH&#41; and the correlation length &#40;CL&#41;, both computed from a digitized snow transect obtained by a digital photograph of a panel vertically inserted into the snow. <br>- &#42;&#42;Snow water equivalent&#42;&#42; was sampled in sections from the surface to the bottom of the snowpack with a cylinder cutter. <br>&amp;nbsp;<br>Additionally, &#42;&#42;runoff&#42;&#42; was automatically measured in the close proximity to the measurement field at a sub-hourly resolution by a lysimeter. The instrument was unfortunately discovered to be clogged at the start of the runoff in 2023 and only repaired in late May 2023. Therefore, the time series is not representative of the runoff start in 2023. The instrument was inspected promptly and assessed as fully functional for the upcoming snow season. The manually measured values of &#42;&#42;SWE&#42;&#42; are complemented by an automatically recorded time series at sub-hourly time intervals with an SSG1000 snow scale manufactured by Sommer Messtechnik, Austria.<br>&amp;nbsp;<br> ---<br>&amp;nbsp;<br>- References:<br>  - HI98501 Checktemp: &#91;https://www.hannainstruments.co.uk/modules/teapotknowledgehub/uploads/ist98501&#95;06&#95;18-60d496ca2cd31.pdf&#93;&#40;https://www.hannainstruments.co.uk/modules/teapotknowledgehub/uploads/ist98501&#95;06&#95;18-60d496ca2cd31.pdf&#41;<br>  - InfraSnow sensor: Wolfsperger, Fabian &amp; Ziegler, Silvio &amp; Schneebeli, Martin &amp; Löwe, Henning. &#40;2022&#41;. ## Load packages

This template targets tidyverse (2.x) and skimr (2.x) with R 4.1 or newer for the native `|>` pipe; package versions are not pinned. Install missing packages once with `install.packages(c("tidyverse", "skimr"))`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(skimr)
theme_set(theme_minimal())

USER_AGENT <- "OpendataSwiss-StarterCode-R/1.0"
HTTP_TIMEOUT <- 30

get_dataset <- function(url, delim = NULL, drop_empty_unnamed = TRUE, ...) {
  if (grepl("^https?://", url)) {
    local_file <- tempfile()
    on.exit(unlink(local_file), add = TRUE)
    old_options <- options(timeout = HTTP_TIMEOUT)
    on.exit(options(old_options), add = TRUE)
    status <- download.file(url, local_file, method = "libcurl", mode = "wb",
                            quiet = TRUE, headers = c("User-Agent" = USER_AGENT))
    if (status != 0) stop("Resource download failed")
    url <- local_file
  }
  data <- read_delim(url, delim = delim, show_col_types = FALSE, ...)
  stop_for_problems(data)
  if (drop_empty_unnamed && nrow(data) > 0) {
    # Blank CSV headers (often from trailing separators) become "...n".
    unnamed <- grepl("^\\.\\.\\.[0-9]+$", names(data))
    empty_unnamed <- unnamed & map_lgl(data, ~ all(is.na(.x)))
    if (any(empty_unnamed)) {
      message("Removed empty unnamed columns: ", paste(names(data)[empty_unnamed], collapse = ", "))
      data <- data[, !empty_unnamed, drop = FALSE]
    }
  }
  data
}
```

## Load data

Selected resource: **6ca91588-fc57-4b83-9220-4971ed2f9656** (CSV). This notebook loads only this resource.

For CSV, the delimiter and column types are guessed. Check the preview and metadata; set `delim`, `col_types`, `na`, or `locale` in `get_dataset(...)` when needed (for example, read identifiers with leading zeros as character columns). Parsing problems stop the import so they can be addressed.

Fully empty columns named `...n` are removed on import. Named empty columns and unnamed columns containing values are kept. Use `drop_empty_unnamed = FALSE` to retain every column, including intentionally named `...n` fields.

## Missing values

```{r missing-values}
missing <- tibble(
  column = names(df),
  missing = map_int(df, ~ sum(is.na(.x))),
  missing_pct = map_dbl(df, ~ mean(is.na(.x)) * 100)
) |>
  arrange(desc(missing_pct))
missing

# Show up to 20 columns with missing values; percentages use all rows.
missing_plot <- missing |> filter(missing > 0) |> slice_head(n = 20)
if (nrow(missing_plot) > 0) {
  ggplot(missing_plot, aes(x = missing_pct, y = reorder(column, missing_pct))) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(x = "Missing values (%)", y = NULL, title = "Missingness by column")
} else {
  message("No missing values to plot (or the dataset has no rows).")
}
```

## Summary and distributions

`skim()` reports completeness and type-specific summaries. Inspect units before interpreting numeric codes as measurements.

```{r summary}
if (nrow(df) > 0 && ncol(df) > 0) {
  skim(df)
} else {

}
```

```{r histograms}
# Plot up to four numeric columns, excluding non-finite values only from plots.
numeric_names <- names(select(df, where(is.numeric))) |> head(4)
for (column in numeric_names) {
  values <- df[[column]]
  values <- values[is.finite(values)]
  if (length(values) > 0) {
    plot <- ggplot(tibble(value = values), aes(x = value)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
      labs(title = column, x = column, y = "Count")
    print(plot)
  }
}
```

```{r category-counts}
# Top 10 values for up to three categorical columns, including missing values.
categorical_names <- df |>
  select(where(~ is.character(.x) || is.factor(.x) || is.logical(.x))) |>
  names() |>
  head(3)
for (column in categorical_names) {
  cat(column, "\n")
  df |> count(.data[[column]], sort = TRUE) |> head(10) |> print()
}
```
